title.en: US military says it disabled tanker trying to breach blockade amid new wave of strikes on Iran – Middle East crisis live
title.zh: 美国军方称在对伊朗的新一轮袭击中，击毁一艘试图突破封锁的油轮——中东危机直播

summary.en: The US military reported disabling an oil tanker attempting to breach a blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, using missile strikes. This incident occurred during a fourth consecutive day of US strikes on Iran, with former President Trump also issuing threats against Iranian power plants.

In the recent attacks on the southern part of the country, more than 30 civilians lost their lives. While expressing our condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families, we honour the memory of the fallen. The government will stand by the people with all its might. The south of Iran is the beating heart of this land. The south of Iran, the soul of Iran.” Continue reading...

title.en: A Cold War bunker gets a luxury makeover as 'doomsday' condos
title.zh: 冷战时期的地堡被豪华改造为“世界末日”公寓

summary.en: A former Canadian government nuclear bomb shelter in rural Nova Scotia may soon be home to the country’s first large-scale luxury survival shelter.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
"From here to anywhere" is the motto of Debert's business park, but it feels like the middle of nowhere.

Just 113km (70 miles) north of Halifax, Nova Scotia, on Canada's east coast, it was once a military base where thousands of soldiers trained during World War Two. Now it's a mix old buildings and empty parking lots, bordered by thin, coniferous woods.

But there is promise of a luxurious and glamorous future in the large grassy hump popping up at one end of the park.

Canadian crypto mogul Jonathan Baha'i plans to convert the 64,000 square-foot nuclear bomb shelter into crisis-proof condos where billionaires can ride out all sorts of cataclysm.

The 50-unit project, managed by Baha'is Fallout Complex Inc, will offer amenities such as gourmet dining from a "self-sustaining" food source, biometric access, around-the-clock surveillance, and onsite medical services. Tenants with private planes can land at the small Debert Airport nearby.

After buying the site, commonly called The Diefenbunker, in 2013 for C$31,300 ($22,000; £16,500), Baha'i first pursued a different business model for it that included laser tag and historical tours, along with a small data centre.

"There's more uncertainty in the world in the last two years than in the last 30 years," Paul Mansfield, a project co-owner, told the local council last autumn. "It sort of led to a rebirth of people wanting to have an insurance policy" - a 'doomsday bunker'."

The company will work with German firm Bespoke Home and Yacht Security, which Mansfield said had provided security for US Vice-President JD Vance and reality star Kim Kardashian, though their client list is not public.

Bespoke's recommended measures for the forthcoming complex, which has already sold 11 units, include flying drones to survey its perimeter, according to Mansfield.

The renovation plans also include a spa, a yoga room, and a cigar lounge. Modern OLED lights will replicate natural light, and an adjacent overground bunker will be used to grow food.

When condo owners aren't there, the units will be rented out for hotel stays and the profits will be shared. Both the cost to buy and the cost to rent are secret.

"If somebody was renting it as a hotel room and something happened and they had to get kicked out, they would get kicked out," Mansfield said.

Former Canadian Prime Minister John Diefenbaker had seven bunkers built across the country from the late 1950s to the mid-1960s, meant to house a skeleton crew of government officials in the event of nuclear war.

The bunker in Debert was designed to withstand a near-hit from a nuclear explosion and sustain 329 people for at least 30 days.

But by the time the bunkers were complete, they were already obsolete - long-range missile targeting had advanced and nuclear bombs...
body.zh: “从这里到任何地方”是德伯特商业园的座右铭，但它感觉就像是一个偏僻的地方。 它位于加拿大东海岸新斯科舍省哈利法克斯以北 113 公里（70 英里）处，曾是第二次世界大战期间数千名士兵接受训练的军事基地。现在这里是古老建筑和空停车场的混合体，周围是稀疏的针叶林。 但在公园一端突然出现的巨大草丛中，有望打造出奢华而迷人的未来。 加拿大加密货币大亨乔纳森·巴哈伊 (Jonathan Baha'i) 计划将 64,000 平方英尺的核防空洞改造成防危机公寓，亿万富翁可以在这里安然度过各种灾难。 这个拥有 50 个单元的项目由 Baha'is Fallout Complex Inc 管理，将提供各种便利设施，例如来自“自给自足”食物来源的美食、生物识别访问、全天候监控和现场医疗服务。拥有私人飞机的租户可以降落在附近的小型德伯特机场。 2013 年，巴哈伊以 31,300 加元（22,000 美元；16,500 英镑）购买了这个通常称为迪芬邦克 (The Diefenbunker) 的网站后，巴哈伊首先为其寻求一种不同的商业模式，包括激光标签和历史之旅，以及一个小型数据中心。 项目共同所有人保罗·曼斯菲尔德 (Paul Mansfield) 去年秋天对当地议会表示：“过去两年世界的不确定性比过去 30 年还要多。” “这在某种程度上导致了那些想要拥有保险单的人的重生”——“世界末日地堡”。” 该公司将与德国公司 Bespoke Home and Yacht Security 合作，曼斯菲尔德表示，该公司为美国副总统 JD Vance 和真人秀明星金·卡戴珊 (Kim Kardashian) 提供安全保障，不过他们的客户名单并未公开。 Mansfield 表示，Bespoke 为即将建成的综合体建议采取的措施包括使用无人机对其周边进行勘察，该综合体已售出 11 套。 改造计划还包括水疗中心、瑜伽室和雪茄休息室。现代 OLED 灯将复制自然光，相邻的地上掩体将用于种植食物。 当公寓业主不在时，这些单位将被出租用于酒店住宿，利润将被分享。购买成本和租赁成本都是秘密的。 曼斯菲尔德说：“如果有人租用它作为酒店房间，并且发生了一些事情，他们不得不被赶出去，他们就会被赶出去。” 加拿大前总理约翰·迪芬贝克 (John Diefenbaker) 从 20 世纪 50 年代末到 1960 年代中期在全国各地建造了七个掩体，旨在在发生核战争时容纳政府官员的骨干人员。 德伯特的掩体设计能够承受核爆炸的险些袭击，并能容纳 329 人至少 30 天。 但当掩体完工时，它们已经过时了——远程导弹瞄准有先进的核弹……

title.en: New monkey species with orange lips found 'hiding' in DRC forest
title.zh: 刚果森林中发现“隐藏”的橙色嘴唇新猴种

summary.en: Scientists describe "amazing feeling" to look into the face of an animal that so few people knew existed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A monkey that has striking pinkish-orange lips and a black face - and lives in the forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo - has been confirmed as a new species to science.

The black-furred primate was spotted and photographed hidden away in the high tree canopy of dense tropical forests in Lomami National Park, in the central east of the country.

Conservationists working there first reported seeing this unusual-looking animal back in 2008. But they captured just one blurry photograph.

After another sighting 10 years later, an international team set out to find and study the monkey and revealed that it was a previously unknown species.

This is only the fifth African monkey species to be discovered in the last 75 years.

Junior Amboko, a PhD student at Florida Atlantic University, played a leading role in the search, which involved audio recordings, photography and detailed genetic studies.

Amboko told BBC News it was an "amazing feeling" to look into the face of an animal that so few people knew existed.

"Discovering" a species, in this context, means officially recording and confirming it has evolved to be genetically distinct. Some local people already knew of the monkey's existence and refer to it by a common name - Likweli.

But Amboko said the monkeys were "kind of shy" - and tended to hide high in the trees.

"As part of our search, we interviewed people in 52 villages close to where the animals live. And only people in eight villages [had ever seen] them," he recalled.

The research team - from DRC, the US and Germany - gave the animal the Latin name Colobus congoensis in recognition of the natural diversity in the country.

It belongs to the larger group of colobus monkeys. "These are really important African monkeys that don't have thumbs," explained Prof Kate Detwiler from Florida Atlantic University.

"They're these herbivores of the canopy that are a critical part of the ecosystem. We think they have a lot to do with processing seeds and germination in the forest."

Prof Detwiler speculates that their unusual, bright facial markings could be a visual signal to other animals, potentially attractive to a mate or that it could allow the animals to identify each other.

The monkeys also have a distinctive "roaring" call. "You often hear them, but don't see them," said Amboko.

They think the animals are rare and restricted to a part of the forest where they can find the food and habitat they need.

The animals are hunted for meat, so the researchers hope that now that Colobus congoensis is classified as a distinct species it can be officially protected.

body.zh: 一种生活在刚果民主共和国森林中、有着引人注目的粉橙色嘴唇和黑色脸庞的猴子已被科学证实为一个新物种。 人们在该国中东部洛马米国家公园茂密热带森林的高树冠中发现并拍摄了这只黑毛灵长类动物的照片。 在那里工作的环保人士早在 2008 年就首次报告称看到了这种长相不寻常的动物。但他们只拍到了一张模糊的照片。 十年后再次目击这只猴子后，一个国际小组开始寻找和研究这只猴子，并发现它是一个以前未知的物种。 这是过去 75 年来发现的第五种非洲猴类。 佛罗里达大西洋大学的博士生朱尼尔·安博科（Junior Amboko）在这次搜寻中发挥了主导作用，其中涉及录音、摄影和详细的基因研究。 安博科告诉英国广播公司新闻，看到一种很少有人知道其存在的动物的脸是一种“奇妙的感觉”。 在这种情况下，“发现”一个物种意味着正式记录并确认它已经进化到具有独特的基因。一些当地人已经知道这种猴子的存在，并给它起了一个常见的名字——Likweli。 但安博科表示，这些猴子“有点害羞”，往往躲在树上的高处。 “作为搜索的一部分，我们采访了动物居住地附近 52 个村庄的人们。只有 8 个村庄的人们[曾经见过]它们，”他回忆道。 来自刚果民主共和国、美国和德国的研究小组给这种动物起了拉丁文名字 Colobus congoensis，以表彰该国的自然多样性。 它属于较大的疣猴群体。佛罗里达大西洋大学的凯特·德特怀勒教授解释说：“这些是非常重要的非洲猴子，它们没有拇指。” “它们是树冠上的食草动物，是生态系统的重要组成部分。我们认为它们与森林中种子的加工和发芽有很大关系。” 德特怀勒教授推测，它们不寻常、明亮的面部标记可能是其他动物的视觉信号，可能对配偶有吸引力，或者可以让动物相互识别。 猴子还有独特的“咆哮”叫声。 “你经常听到它们，但看不到它们，”安博科说。 他们认为这些动物很稀有，仅限于森林的一部分，在那里它们可以找到所需的食物和栖息地。 这些动物被猎杀是为了获取肉类，因此研究人员希望刚果疣猴现在被列为一个独特的物种，可以得到正式保护。 研究人员表示，他们对这个新描述的神秘物种仍然有很多疑问。他们计划进行更详细的调查来估计他们的人口并......

title.en: Families of 43 victims await verdict in Genoa bridge disaster
title.zh: 热那亚大桥灾难 43 名遇难者家属等待判决

summary.en: A large section of the giant Morandi motorway bridge crumbled and collapsed on to the railway tracks below.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On the morning of 14 August 2018, Claudia Possetti, 47, was in the car with her new husband Andrea, and her two children, aged 12 and 16.

The couple had just married and were driving to the Italian Riviera with the youngsters for a holiday when the Morandi bridge in the northern city of Genoa collapsed beneath them.

Their car was among those that plunged from the viaduct on to the railway tracks below. The four of them were among 43 people killed in one of Italy's worst infrastructure disasters in decades.

Nearly eight years on, Claudia's sister, Egle Possetti, will be among relatives gathering in a Genoa courtroom on Thursday to hear a first-instance verdict in the trial over the collapse. The children's father, who survived them, is also expected to be in court.

"I feel anxious, worried, very emotional," Egle told the BBC. "After so many years, so many hearings, we may be able to see some light. It would be so important for us to know if someone's been held accountable."

The bridge came down during a summer storm at the height of the holiday season, sending cars and lorries plunging to the ground below.

The collapse triggered years of investigation into how the viaduct, built in the 1960s and part of a key route linking Genoa to the French border, had been allowed to fail.

Fifty-seven people have stood trial since July 2022. Among them are former executives of toll road operator Autostrade per l'Italia and its parent company Atlantia, engineers from the maintenance firm Spea, and former transport ministry officials. The charges range from multiple manslaughter to falsifying documents.

At the heart of the Morandi bridge case is a basic disagreement over why the bridge fell.

Prosecutors say maintenance was repeatedly delayed, even as warning signs were ignored, while profits kept flowing.

Defence lawyers argue the real cause was a design flaw in the specific cable that failed, and that no maintenance regime could have prevented it as it was encased in concrete. Some lesser charges, including document forgery, have already lapsed under Italy's statute of limitations.

Francesco Pinto, the former deputy chief prosecutor who worked on the case, has described the length of the proceedings as symptomatic of deeper problems in Italy's justice system, and believes an appeal and a final Supreme Court ruling could together take another two and a half years.

Giovanni Paolo Accinni, who is defending former Atlantia chief executive Giovanni Castellucci, points instead to the prosecution's lengthy pre-trial technical investigations, much of which he says had to be gone over again once the trial began.

Castellucci is already serving a six-year sentence over another fatal incident on a viaduct in southern Italy which killed 40 people in 2013.

title.en: Argentina face action after waving Falklands banner
title.zh: 阿根廷因挥舞福克兰群岛横幅面临行动

summary.en: Argentina's football team faces potential disciplinary action from Fifa after displaying a banner supporting their country's claim to the Falkland Islands during their World Cup semi-final victory celebration against England.
summary.zh: 阿根廷足球队在世界杯半决赛战胜英格兰后，在庆祝活动中展示了一面支持其国家对福克兰群岛主权主张的横幅，可能面临国际足联的纪律处分。

body.en:
Argentina face the prospect of disciplinary action from Fifa after their players celebrated the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands.

The defending world champions produced a dramatic late comeback in Atlanta, scoring twice to defeat Thomas Tuchel's side 2-1 and book a showdown with Spain in Sunday's final.

After the final whistle, Argentina players celebrated while holding a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine".

The Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory in the south-west Atlantic Ocean, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina.

The two nations went to war over the group of islands, situated 300 miles off Argentina's east coast, from April to June 1982.

The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British servicemen. Three people from the islands also died.

In 2014, Fifa fined the Argentine Football Association £20,000 after its players held up a banner with the same message before a friendly against Slovenia.

World football's governing body said the gesture had breached rules on political action and team misconduct.

After Wednesday's victory, Argentina vice-president Victoria Villarruel posted on X , external , writing "it wasn't just another match" alongside a video of what appeared to be Argentine soldiers.

"The Falklands are Argentine," Villarruel posted. "They banned bringing them to the stadium and forgot that we carry them in our blood and our hearts."

In the build-up to the game, Villarruel had said the semi-final was "about putting the invaders in their place".

Argentina players also sang chants which referenced the Falklands and Argentina greats Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi following their dramatic 3-2 win over Egypt in the last 16.

However, before the semi-final, manager Lionel Scaloni had said he was "not going to mix" football and politics.

"The reality is that this is a football match. I can't mix things up, especially out of respect for what happened so many years ago," Scaloni had said.

"It was a very sad period in our history, and there isn't much we can do about it, that's the reality.

"Things are happening elsewhere in the world, and we criticise the existence of war. We certainly remember those people, of course. But it is a football match - we shouldn't confuse the two."

The semi-final, which England lost to late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez, was held under increased security measures because of the historical tensions between the two nations.
body.zh: 阿根廷队球员在世界杯半决赛战胜英格兰队时举起支持阿根廷对福克兰群岛主权的横幅庆祝，因此他们可能面临国际足联的纪律处分。 卫冕世界冠军在亚特兰大戏剧性地逆转，梅开二度以2-1击败托马斯·图赫尔的球队，并在周日的决赛中与西班牙队对决。 终场哨响后，阿根廷球员举着写着“拉斯马尔维纳斯之子阿根廷人”的横幅庆祝，翻译过来就是“福克兰群岛是阿根廷的”。 福克兰群岛是位于西南大西洋的英国海外领土，仍然是英国和阿根廷之间主权争端的主题。 1982 年 4 月至 6 月，两国为距阿根廷东海岸 300 英里的群岛发生战争。 持续74天的冲突导致655名阿根廷军人和255名英国军人死亡。岛上的三人也死亡。 2014年，阿根廷足协因球员在与斯洛文尼亚的友谊赛前举起写有相同信息的横幅而被国际足联罚款2万英镑。 世界足球管理机构表示，这一举动违反了政治行动和球队不当行为的规定。 周三获胜后，阿根廷副总统维多利亚·维拉鲁埃尔 (Victoria Villarruel) 在《X》、《外部》上发帖，写道“这不仅仅是另一场比赛”，并附上了一段似乎是阿根廷士兵的视频。 “福克兰群岛是阿根廷的，”维拉鲁埃尔发帖说。 “他们禁止将他们带入体育场，却忘记了我们的血液和心中都带着他们。” 在比赛准备阶段，维拉鲁埃尔表示半决赛的目的是“让入侵者就位”。 阿根廷球员在十六强赛以 3-2 戏剧性战胜埃及后，还唱起了马岛和阿根廷伟大球星迭戈·马拉多纳和莱昂内尔·梅西的圣歌。 然而，在半决赛之前，主教练莱昂内尔·斯卡洛尼曾表示，他“不会将足球和政治混为一谈”。 “现实是，这是一场足球比赛。我不能把事情搞混，尤其是出于对多年前发生的事情的尊重，”斯卡罗尼说道。 “这是我们历史上非常悲伤的时期，我们对此无能为力，这就是现实。 “世界其他地方正在发生一些事情，我们批评战争的存在。当然，我们当然记得那些人。但这是一场足球比赛——我们不应该混淆两者。” 由于恩佐·费尔南德斯和劳塔罗·马丁内斯在最后时刻的进球，英格兰队输给了半决赛，由于两国之间历史上的紧张关系，半决赛是在加强安全措施的情况下举行的。

reflection.en: In moments of national pride, it can be tempting to assert historical claims, yet the call to live peaceably with all people remains. Even in competitive arenas, our actions can either foster unity or reignite old tensions, reminding us of the ongoing effort required for peace.
reflection.zh: 在民族自豪的时刻，人们很容易重申历史主张，然而，与所有人和平相处的呼召依然存在。即使在竞技场上，我们的行为也能促进团结或重新点燃旧的紧张关系，提醒我们为和平所做的持续努力。

title.zh: 美国发动新一轮袭击，特朗普声称伊朗“很快就会被击败”

summary.en: The United States conducted another series of strikes, while former President Trump stated that Iran would soon be defeated. Despite these military actions, formal negotiations between the US and Iran have not concluded.
summary.zh: 美国发动了新一轮袭击，而特朗普声称伊朗“很快就会被击败”。尽管有新一轮袭击，美国和伊朗之间的谈判尚未正式结束。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has claimed that Iran "will be defeated soon", after the US launched a new wave of strikes against Iran on Wednesday in a return to war between the two foes.

The US and Iran have resumed fighting with strikes on targets across the region , less than a month after they signed a memorandum of understanding that aimed at ending the war in the Middle East.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain, claiming it had intercepted attacks against civilian targets.

Jordan, which has a close defence partner with the US, said they had downed three missiles from the Islamic republic.

Several explosions were also heard late Wednesday near the US consulate in Erbil, the capital of Iraq's northern Kurdistan region.

Meanwhile, Trump has threatened to widen strikes next week to include power plants and bridges into US targets, unless Iran returns to the negotiating table.

He also claimed that Iran wanted to settle with the US, but the US would decide if they would want a settlement.

Iran blockaded Hormuz after the war erupted with US-Israeli strikes on 28 February , using the waterway for leverage against its foes for months.

The strait was briefly reopened after the US-Iran deal last month, before Tehran vowed last week it would be closed again "until the US ends its aggression".

Traffic through the waterway remained low, with maritime tracker Kpler reporting only 21 transits on Tuesday.

The US has reimposed its own blockade of Iran's ports. On Thursday, the US Central Command said its military disabled an unladen oil tanker attempting to sail toward an Iranian port.

"The commercial vessel ignored multiple warnings as it attempted to violate the US blockade. A US aircraft disabled the vessel after firing hellfire missiles into the ship's smokestack,” it said.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the renewed US blockade "has, in a way, dismantled the Islamabad memorandum", referring to the interim deal reached last month.

Despite renewed hostilities, mediated talks between the two sides have not formally ended .

But Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told state television on Wednesday that "a memorandum of understanding only has meaning when its clauses are valid and being implemented. If Iran is not to derive any benefit from the memorandum of understanding, we have no reason to adhere".

Since last week, renewed US attacks have killed at least 30 people in Iran, government spokesman Fatemeh Mohajerani said.

title.en: Kenya: Court rejects Rastafari bid for religious freedom marijuana exemption
title.zh: 肯尼亚：法院驳回拉斯塔法里宗教自由大麻豁免的请求

summary.en: Kenya's small Rastafarian community was seeking legal permission to smoke marijuana under the constitutional right to freedom of religion. The judge found they did not show it to be a necessary part of their worship.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 肯尼亚的拉斯塔法里教小社区正在根据宪法宗教自由权寻求吸食大麻的法律许可。法官发现他们没有表明这是他们崇拜的必要组成部分。 周三，肯尼亚一家法院以宗教理由拒绝授予拉斯特法里教徒吸食大麻的权利，此前该少数派宗教人士寻求豁免该国根植于英国殖民统治的严厉毒品法。 拉斯特法里教徒经常使用大麻作为他们所谓的宗教冥想的一部分，自 2021 年以来一直在敦促肯尼亚法院批准他们使用这种草药。 他们认为，宗教自由的宪法权利应该受到保护。 内罗毕的肯尼亚高等法院裁定，该社区未能在听证会上证明大麻是其宗教活动的必要组成部分，因此没有授予他们绕过该国禁毒法的权利。 法官巴哈蒂·姆瓦穆耶 (Bahati Mwamuye) 表示，虽然所有证人“都同意大麻被用作圣礼，但他们无法就大麻的使用是否必要或仅仅是首选达成一致”。 该社区的律师 Shadrack Wambui 表示，他们计划对该决定提出上诉。 尽管周三对具体案件做出了不利于该案件的裁决，但姆​​瓦穆耶法官表示，肯尼亚应该就其毒品政策举行更广泛的全国辩论。 “这不仅是拉斯塔法里社区的问题，也是整个社会的问题，”他说。 法官补充道：“毫无疑问，大麻的使用在这个国家已经变得无处不在，而且可以说几十年来一直如此。”他甚至引用了彼得·托什（Peter Tosh）的开创性雷鬼歌曲“合法化它”，包括歌词：“法官吸大麻，甚至律师也吸。” 肯尼亚拥有严格的禁毒法，其中许多法律的根源可以追溯到 20 世纪初殖民国家英国的立法。 持有和吸食大麻可处以最高 2,000 美元的罚款（根据人均 GDP 计算，远远超过平均收入者 6 个月的工资）、最高 10 年的监禁，或两者并罚。与贩运或种植植物有关的犯罪可能面临更严厉的处罚。 姆瓦穆耶表示，“现状似乎站不住脚”，并认为应该“就大麻以及我们应该采取的方向进行全面和坦诚的对话。” 拉斯塔法里教于 20 世纪 30 年代在牙买加形成，大多数人认为它是基于对基督教圣经的解释。 它与反抗殖民文化和英国统治有很强的联系，并深受埃塞俄比亚主义和回到非洲运动的影响。 它对前埃塞俄比亚皇帝海尔·塞拉西（Haile Selassie）的崇拜，无论是作为先知还是......

title.en: India-linked organized crime gangs pose global challenge
title.zh: 与印度有关的有组织犯罪团伙构成全球挑战

summary.en: The Bishnoi case shows how India-based transnational organized crime networks have evolved into a global law enforcement concern.
summary.zh: 比什诺伊案表明，总部设在印度的跨国有组织犯罪网络已演变为全球执法部门关注的问题。

body.en:
The Bishnoi case shows how India-based transnational organized crime networks have evolved into a global law enforcement concern.

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) called it "Operation Hard Ball" — the largest international crackdown yet on India -based organized crime gangs.  

Last week, it led to the arrest of 24 suspects across the US, Canada and Spain and the indictment of 37 defendants.

At its center was Lawrence Bishnoi, a jailed Indian gangster whom US prosecutors accuse of directing murders, extortion and international drug trafficking from inside a prison in Gujarat state using smuggled mobile phones.

His alleged deputy, Goldy Brar, also known as Satinderjeet Singh Brar, remains a fugitive with a $50,000 (€43,735) FBI reward on his head.

India on Tuesday welcomed the US indictment of Bishnoi and several associates over the 2023 killing of Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada , saying the case underscored the growing threat posed by transnational organized crime.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India and the US shared a "strong and growing" partnership in combating organized crime and terrorism.

But experts say the significance of Operation Hard Ball extends far beyond one gang. It reveals how India-based organized crime gangs have evolved from a domestic law-and-order problem into a transnational criminal enterprise spanning North America, Europe and beyond.

According to the indictment, the Bishnoi organization used violence, drug trafficking and extortion to build influence among the Indian diaspora.

Prosecutors allege the gang demanded millions of dollars from business owners in North America and ordered acts of violence against those who refused to pay.

The indictment also accuses Bishnoi and Brar of directing the 2023 killing of Nijjar outside a gurdwara (Sikhs' place of worship) in Surrey, British Columbia — a murder that plunged India-Canada relations into crisis. The charging document, however, does not allege any Indian government involvement in the killing.

In the 1980s and 1990s, Indian gangster Dawood Ibrahim created a transnational organized crime syndicate — called the D-Company — operating from Dubai and later Karachi, using smuggling, narcotics and extortion networks that stretched across Asia, the Gulf and Europe.

His former lieutenant, Chhota Rajan, built a rival network across Southeast Asia before his arrest in Indonesia in 2015. Those syndicates relied on geographical safe havens, political protection and tightly controlled hierarchies.

title.en: Iran: Alleged Ahmadinejad plot highlights info war
title.zh: 伊朗：据称艾哈迈迪-内贾德的阴谋凸显信息战

summary.en: Reports suggest Israel explored a scenario to effect regime change in Iran involving former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, revealing how the Iran war has also become a struggle over narratives and perception.
summary.zh: 有报道称，以色列曾考虑一项涉及伊朗前总统马哈茂德·艾哈迈迪-内贾德的政权更迭方案，这表明伊朗战争已演变为一场关于叙事和认知的“信息战”。

body.en:
Reports that Israel explored a scenario to effect regime change involving former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad reveal how the Iran war has also become a struggle over narratives and perception.

Two separate reports, one published recently by The New York Times  in the US and the other by Israeli daily  Haaretz , have reignited debate over Israel's thinking about regime change in Iran.  

They have also raised questions over the role of ultraconservative former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad — who served two terms from 2005 to 2013 — in Iranian politics.

According to the reports, Israeli officials allegedly explored installing Ahmadinejad as a possible figurehead in a post-Islamic Republic scenario, with efforts reportedly intensifying during the war and involving secret contacts in Hungary.

The reports have attracted attention partly because of their sensational details.

They claim that Ahmadinejad was moved to a safe house after his compound was hit by an Israeli air strike on February 28, 2026, and that David Barnea, the former chief of Israel's Mossad intelligence service, personally oversaw part of the contact effort, which reportedly included a meeting in Budapest.

Haaretz also wrote that the operation involved much more than Ahmadinejad and included infiltration plans inside Iran, contacts with minority groups and that there was also discussion of a broader destabilization strategy.

The details have not been independently verified and remain unconfirmed. However, Ahmadinejad's office has reportedly rejected the claims, describing them as "absurd" and "completely false."

Babak Dorbeiki, a London-based political analyst and former official at Iran's Strategic Research Center, told DW that the first task was now to separate three different questions: the accuracy of the reporting itself, Ahmadinejad's real place in Iranian politics today and the political function of publishing such stories.

"There is no public and independent evidence that can conclusively confirm or reject the details of this narrative," he said. "So it can neither be accepted without question nor simply dismissed because it has been denied."

Dorbeiki argued that Ahmadinejad still had a social base and considerable unmistakable political ambition, but that this should not be confused with real power.

In his view, the former president has been pushed away from the core institutions of the Islamic Republic since roughly 2010, including the Office of the Supreme Leader , the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the Guardian Council and much of the conservative camp.

body.zh: 有报道称，以色列探索了一种涉及伊朗前总统内贾德的政权更迭方案，揭示了伊朗战争如何成为一场叙事和看法之争。 两份独立的报告，一份由美国《纽约时报》最近发表，另一份由以色列日报《国土报》发表，重新引发了关于以色列对伊朗政权更迭的看法的争论。 他们还对极端保守的前总统马哈茂德·艾哈迈迪内贾德（Mahmoud Ahmadinejad）——2005 年至 2013 年连任两届——在伊朗政治中的作用提出了质疑。 据报道，以色列官员据称曾考虑在后伊斯兰共和国的情况下任命艾哈迈迪内贾德为可能的傀儡，据报道，这一努力在战争期间加剧，并涉及匈牙利的秘密接触。 这些报道之所以引起关注，部分原因在于其耸人听闻的细节。 他们声称，艾哈迈迪内贾德的住所于 2026 年 2 月 28 日遭到以色列空袭后被转移到安全屋，以色列摩萨德情报部门前负责人戴维·巴尼亚 (David Barnea) 亲自监督了部分联络工作，据报道其中包括在布达佩斯举行的一次会议。 《国土报》还写道，这次行动涉及的不仅仅是艾哈迈迪内贾德，还包括伊朗境内的渗透计划、与少数群体的接触，以及更广泛的破坏稳定战略的讨论。 详细信息尚未经过独立核实，仍未得到证实。然而，据报道，内贾德办公室否认了这些说法，称其“荒谬”且“完全错误”。 驻伦敦的政治分析师、伊朗战略研究中心前官员巴巴克·多尔贝基 (Babak Dorbeiki) 告诉德国之声，现在的首要任务是区分三个不同的问题：报道本身的准确性、艾哈迈迪内贾德在当今伊朗政治中的真实地位以及发表此类报道的政治功能。 “没有公开和独立的证据可以最终证实或否认这一叙述的细节，”他说。 “因此，它既不能毫无疑问地被接受，也不能因为被否认而简单地驳回。” 多贝基认为，艾哈迈迪内贾德仍然拥有社会基础和相当大的明确的政治野心，但这不应与真正的权力相混淆。 在他看来，这位前总统自 2010 年左右以来就被逐出伊斯兰共和国的核心机构，包括最高领袖办公室、伊斯兰革命卫队 (IRGC)、监护委员会和大部分保守派阵营。 多尔贝基说，艾哈迈迪内贾德在最近的总统选举中一再被取消竞选资格，这表明伊朗的关键人物在发号施令……

title.en: Kenya's 'political gangs' fuel election fears
title.zh: 肯尼亚的“政治帮派”加剧选举担忧

summary.en: Violent disruptions of political and civic events are raising concerns about the use of hired gangs as Kenya heads toward elections in 2027.
summary.zh: 随着肯尼亚迈向2027年大选，政治和公民活动中发生的暴力骚乱，引发了人们对雇佣帮派行为的担忧。

body.en:
Violent disruptions of political and civic events are raising concerns about the use of hired gangs as Kenya heads toward elections in 2027.

For Brian Ongore, a resident of Kenya's capital, Nairobi, seeing groups of young men in public has become a source of anxiety rather than an ordinary part of city life.

"Whenever you see a group of youths, you're just in panic because you never know what will happen to you next," Ongore told DW. "Everybody is in constant panic. The general feeling of safety has gone down. It's like you're living in the jungle."

His concerns echo growing fears among many Kenyans, particularly since recent violent disruptions at opposition-linked gatherings in the towns of Kisumu and Nyahururu.

Increasingly, so-called "goons" are being hired, dozens or even hundreds at a time, to intimidate rivals or disrupt public events ahead of the elections, which are scheduled to take place on August 10, 2027. In a recent report, the French news agency Agence France-Presse (AFP) noted that police often turn a blind eye.

In June, a civil society and church forum at Nairobi's All Saints Cathedral was disrupted during discussions on public finance management.

According to a statement published on Monday by Amnesty International Kenya, the "goons publicly confessed to having been sent by some powerful government officials to carry out the heinous attack."

AFP reported that "Kenyan politicians are hiring armed thugs for as little as $4 per day as poverty and ruthless political competition threaten to unleash uncontrollable violence ahead of elections next year." 

Nairobi businesswoman Priscilla Njoroge urged young Kenyans not to allow themselves to be exploited for political violence. "I would like to tell the goons who are being misused not to play with the peace we have because violence destroys everything. The losses are much greater," she told DW.

University student Paul Mwai also questioned the response of the security agencies, while speaking to DW. "Yesterday police were seen protecting the goons. I have not seen even a single goon being dealt with decisively by the same government that keeps issuing threats," he said.

Speaking at the funeral of Zipporah Kosgey, the wife of veteran Kenyan politician Henry Kosgey last month, Kenyan President William Ruto acknowledged the growing presence of political gangs and warned that violence could undermine the democratic process.

"These goons are innocent children who are being used by bankrupt politicians. They go around causing chaos, assaulting people and causing destruction," Ruto said. "All the goons should be dealt with firmly, and those who are paying these young people should also be tracked down."

title.en: Deadly avian flu detected in New Zealand for the first time
title.zh: 新西兰首次发现致命禽流感

summary.en: The alert followed a migratory seabird near Wellington returning a postive test result.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
New Zealand has reported its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu after a migratory seabird found on a ‌beach near Wellington tested positive.

The case in a ‌brown skua seabird comes after the virus was detected in June in Australia , the last continent to ‌report the virus.

The virulent H5 strain has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions and infecting poultry and dairy farms as well as some farm workers.

"There is no evidence of any mass mortality in wildlife or transmission between wild birds in New Zealand. There has been no detection ‌in poultry," Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said in ⁠a statement on Wednesday.

Hoggard said New Zealand might see a similar pattern to cases reported in Australia , where there have been 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu as of Wednesday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

New Zealand has been preparing for the arrival of H5N1, working with the poultry industry to develop biosecurity and resilience plans.

New Zealand's wild birds are unusually vulnerable because they evolved for millions ⁠of years without native land mammals, leaving many species ‌flightless, ground-nesting and poorly equipped to defend themselves against predators.

That isolation made them unique but also left them highly exposed to habitat ‌loss and introduced pests such as stoats, rats and feral cats.

Many species are already endangered, putting them at great risk of extinction if the virus spreads rapidly.

Health officials have started a vaccination program for 300 core breeding birds from five of the country's most endangered species, including flightless takahe and kakapo.

Brett Gartrell, professor of wildlife health at Massey University, told Reuters ‌he was worried that bird flu could push some of the country's critically endangered birds to extinction.

"We are incredibly worried about New Zealand's biodiversity because our birds have never had to deal with anything like this before," Gartrell said.

"If it spreads quickly in New Zealand, we could be in trouble ... those core group of birds that (officials) want to protect with the vaccination won't be fully immune if it spreads too quickly."

title.en: What happens next in the Strait of Hormuz could set a dangerous precedent
title.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡的下一步行动可能树立危险先例

summary.en: Experts warn that the ongoing dispute over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route, could establish a perilous new standard for how global chokepoints are utilized in future international conflicts.
summary.zh: 专家警告称，围绕霍尔木兹海峡这一重要航道的持续争端，可能会为未来国际冲突中全球咽喉要道的使用方式树立危险的新标准。

body.en:
A fundamental shift in the war in the Middle East means Iran's nuclear capability is no longer at the centre of the conflict, experts say.

Instead, attention is increasingly focused on one of the world's most strategic waterways, the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil flows.

The United States resumed strikes on Iranian targets last week after a tentative memorandum of understanding (MOU) broke down , and on Wednesday, its naval blockade of Iranian ports and the strait was reinstated.

On Tuesday, United States President Donald Trump floated the idea of charging vessels a 20 per cent fee to pass through the strait, which he has now scrapped after searing pushback from the United Nations' shipping agency and others.

Over the past week, Iran has struck seven commercial ships for attempting to pass the contested waterway along routes it has not authorised, US Central Command has said, leading to nearly a dozen sailors being killed, injured, or missing.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said two "offending" supertankers had been hit and disabled after ignoring repeated warnings in the strait. They added on Wednesday that the US was making a "mistake" by assuming reimposing the blockade it lifted in June would force them to negotiate.

The Strait of Hormuz is not only a vital oil route. Disruption to shipping since the war began five months ago has also restricted supplies of fertiliser, helium and other industrial and medical essentials, pushing up food and fuel costs worldwide.

David Smith, an associate professor of American politics and foreign policy at the University of Sydney's United States Studies Centre, told SBS News the developments over the last few days have been a dramatic demonstration that the war's parameters have shifted.

"The original issue about Iran's nuclear program now just seems completely remote," he said.

At the outbreak of the war, the US claimed to be seeking a permanent end to Iran's nuclear ambitions, the destruction of its military, and the end to support for regional proxies like Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Iran has maintained its nuclear program is for civilian energy purposes, not weapons development.

While Trump has frequently repeated his demand that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon — and threatened to strike a suspected nuclear site in north-central Iran known as Pickaxe Mountain on Tuesday — the MoU he signed in June deferred a decision over Iran's nuclear program while attempting to immediately resolve the Strait of Hormuz issue.

title.en: 'Completely disfigured': Wife recalls experience as husband sucked out of Ryanair plane
title.zh: “完全毁容”：妻子回忆丈夫被瑞安航空飞机吸出机舱的经历

summary.en: Both Greek prosecutors and air accident investigators have launched investigations into how a window became dislodged on a Ryanair plane, an incident during which a husband was reportedly sucked out and left "completely disfigured."
summary.zh: 希腊检察官和航空事故调查人员已对瑞安航空一架飞机窗户脱落的事件展开调查，据报道，在此事件中，一名丈夫被吸出机舱，导致“完全毁容”。

body.en:
Svetlana Maksimovic and her husband Ljubisa Karovic had ‌just settled into a Ryanair flight when a loud bang pierced the hum of engines.

Within seconds, she saw her 61-year-old husband being ‌sucked out of the plane through a dislodged cabin window.

In what Greek officials have described as a rare incident, Karovic, sitting in a window seat, was pulled through the window as his wife and others held on to him on the flight between the Greek city of Thessaloniki and Germany on 10 July.

"I've never heard anything louder in my life before. I just turned around and saw ‌that part of ‌his body had ⁠already gone out the window," Maksimovic told Reuters.

Karovic is now being treated in hospital in Thessaloniki with severe neck and arm injuries.

Greek media and airport sources said that a piece of engine likely broke off and smashed a window early in the flight, causing the cabin to decompress.

Boeing says it's assisting the investigation, being led by North Macedonia, over which the incident occurred.

The US National Transportation Safety Board and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency are involved in the investigation.

A Greek prosecutor has also launched a probe into the ⁠case, while Greek air accident investigators are also looking into it. The aircraft is still ‌in Greece.

"What happened was extremely serious," ‌the couple's legal adviser, Vassilis Tsiaras, said, adding that the pending results of the probe were pivotal.

Ryanair, which has confirmed that a window dislodged during the flight, said it would not comment further while the incident is under formal investigation.

After takeoff, Karovic was relaxed and had probably fallen asleep, Maksimovic said.

She said that after the loud bang occurred, a woman sitting next to her husband kept pulling his left arm but it was only after another passenger came to help that ‌they succeeded in getting him back inside the plane, which had by then started to descend.

Maksimovic, who had left her seat to help her husband, put an oxygen mask on him while another passenger gave her one for her own use.

"His face was completely disfigured, there was blood everywhere and his ears, eyes, nose were completely deformed," she said, adding that her husband was still struggling to recover.

"How we're going to heal and how long that treatment will last and in what way, we'll see."

title.en: 'I must get out into the free world', dissident who fled China on boat tells BBC
title.zh: 乘船逃离中国的持不同政见者告诉BBC：“我必须进入自由世界”

summary.en: Dong Guangping, who has resettled in Canada, recounts his perilous escape from China to South Korea.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As the rubber boat he was on rocked through choppy waves, fear washed over Chinese dissident Dong Guangping, who had gone without sleep for two days.

The 68-year-old knew he was taking a huge risk trying to flee China by sea, but even then, he had underestimated the challenges of this journey.

He was badly sunburned, his phone was running out of battery, and his portable charger had gone flat. Apart from the sky and the sea, there were no landmarks around him. He could only hope that the digital compass would get him to South Korea before his phone went flat.

"Not being able to navigate would have been terrifying. I could have drifted back towards China," Dong told BBC Chinese nearly two months after his perilous escape.

Forty hours after setting out from China's eastern Shandong province, Dong was rescued by the coast guard and fishermen in Korean waters on the night of 27 May.

He was briefly detained in South Korea but has since resettled in Canada, where his family had been living.

"I can never survive in China," said Dong, who spoke to BBC Chinese in a video call from Toronto.

"If I didn't leave, I will never be at peace for the rest of my life. I had to show the Chinese Communist Party I was capable of leaving. They cannot stop me, they cannot control me."

When asked for comment, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry told the BBC that the Chinese government "handles the entry and exit of its citizens in accordance with the law and that Chinese citizens must abide by the Constitution and the law".

Dong, a police officer-turned-human rights activist, has been jailed in China several times for his activism.

In 1999, Dong was fired from the police force after 13 years because he signed a petition to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the brutal Tiananmen crackdown on pro-democracy protesters .

Then in 2001, he was imprisoned for three years for "inciting subversion of state power". He was jailed again in 2014 for participating in another Tiananmen commemoration event, according to Amnesty International.

Dong had fled China four times previously but was sent back each time. "But I have always held fast to one conviction: I must get out into the free world," he tells BBC Chinese.

In September 2015, he travelled to Bangkok with his wife and daughter, where they were granted refugee status by the United Nations and approved for resettlement in Canada.

But days before they were scheduled to leave for Canada, Thai authorities deported Dong to China , where he was jailed for "inciting subversion" and "crossing the national border illegally". He was sentenced to three and a half years in jail.

body.zh: 当中国异见人士董广平乘坐的橡皮艇在波涛汹涌的海浪中摇晃时，他已经两天没有睡觉了。 这位68岁的老人知道他正冒着巨大的风险试图通过海路逃离中国，但即便如此，他还是低估了这段旅程的挑战。 他被严重晒伤，手机没电了，便携式充电器也没电了。除了天空和大海，他的周围没有任何地标。他只能希望数字指南针能在他的手机没电之前把他带到韩国。 “如果无法导航，那就太可怕了。我可能会漂回中国，”在危险逃亡近两个月后，董告诉 BBC 中文频道。 5月27日晚，董从中国东部山东省出发40小时后，在韩国海域被海警和渔民救起。 他在韩国被短暂拘留，但后来在加拿大定居，他的家人一直居住在那里。 “我永远无法在中国生存，”董在多伦多通过视频通话接受 BBC 中文版采访时说道。 “如果我不离开，我的余生都不会安宁。我必须向中国共产党证明我有能力离开。他们无法阻止我，他们无法控制我。” 当被问及置评时，中国外交部发言人告诉BBC，中国政府“依法办理公民出入境，中国公民必须遵守宪法和法律”。 董曾是一名警察，后来成为人权活动家，他在中国因其活动而多次入狱。 1999年，董因在一份请愿书上签名，纪念天安门残酷镇压民主抗议者10周年，在任职13年后被警察部队开除。 2001年，他因“煽动颠覆国家政权罪”被判入狱三年。据国际特赦组织称，2014 年，他因参加另一场天安门纪念活动而再次入狱。 此前，董曾四次逃离中国，但每次都被遣返。 “但我一直坚守一个信念：我必须走出去，进入自由世界，”他告诉BBC中文网。 2015年9月，他与妻子和女儿一起前往曼谷，在那里他们获得了联合国的难民身份，并获准在加拿大重新定居。 但在他们计划前往加拿大的前几天，泰国当局将董驱逐到中国，并以“煽动颠覆国家政权”和“非法越境”罪名入狱。他被判处三年半监禁。 2019年获释后，他再次试图游向台湾小岛金门越狱，但被中国人救起……

title.en: More people around the world now favour China over the US, Pew study suggests
title.zh: 皮尤研究显示，全球更多人青睐中国而非美国

summary.en: A Pew study indicates that more people globally now favor China over the United States, with greater confidence expressed in President Xi Jinping than in former President Donald Trump.
summary.zh: 皮尤研究中心的一项调查显示，目前全球更多人青睐中国而非美国，对习近平主席的信心也高于唐纳德·特朗普前总统。

body.en:
China is now viewed more positively than the US in many countries around the world, according to a new study by the Pew Research Center. It is the first time the organisation has recorded such results.

The findings from the non-partisan, US-based think tank indicate that favourable views of China have reached record highs in many countries, while perceptions of the United States have worsened.

In general, respondents expressed low confidence in both US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, though Xi scored higher than Trump.

While the US was still seen to respect personal freedoms more than China, China was seen to interfere in other countries' affairs less than the US.

Respondents were asked if they had a very favourable, somewhat favourable, somewhat unfavourable, or very unfavourable opinion of each superpower.

The research centre found that in 25 of the 36 countries, there were more people who had favourable views of China than of the US.

It marks the first time the centre, which has been tracking global sentiments towards the superpowers since 2002, has seen such a result in so many countries, according to Jonathan Schulman, one of the study's researchers.

Pew has seen previous dips in positive views of the US - in 2008, at the end of George Bush's administration, and in 2017, at the start of Trump's first term.

Even then, however, favourable views of China tended to be on par or slightly lower, Schulman told the BBC.

Spain, Indonesia, Italy, Greece and Canada were among the countries that saw the biggest swings towards China.

Only six countries in this year's survey still favour the US more, most of which are staunch US allies: Poland, the Philippines, South Korea, India, Japan and Israel.

Separately, the centre found that the median favourable opinion of the US across 20 countries had dropped steadily in recent years while the median favourable opinion of China had been rising.

Researchers also found that favourable views of China had increased in more than a third of the countries surveyed in recent years, based on an expanded dataset including the US.

And positive views of China reached record highs in some places surveyed this year, including Italy, Spain, Colombia, Mexico, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Turkey.

Researchers found that in general, middle-income countries tended to have positive views of China while wealthier countries tended to have more negative views.

One exception to this pattern was Singapore, which had the highest GDP per capita of the countries surveyed and a high level of positivity towards China.

The most positive - and the most negative - views of China in the survey came from the Asia-Pacific. About 90% of Pakistanis appear to favour China, while just 11% of Japanese do.

title.en: Five arrested after Hong Kong police raid independent bookshops
title.zh: 香港警方突击搜查独立书店后逮捕五人

summary.en: Hong Kong police have arrested five individuals following raids on independent bookshops, alleging they sold "seditious" books that incited "hatred" against authorities.
summary.zh: 香港警方突击搜查独立书店后逮捕了五人，指控他们涉嫌销售煽动对当局“仇恨”的“煽动性”书籍。

body.en:
Five people suspected of selling and displaying books deemed "seditious" in Hong Kong have been arrested after police raided two independent bookshops.

Authorities said the publications incited "hatred" against the territory's government, judiciary and law enforcement agencies. Officers seized books from both shops, the government said in a statement.

The group - two men aged 37 and 57, and three women aged between 30 and 59 - are suspected of violating national security legislation by "acting with seditious intent".

They are currently being held for investigation. If convicted, they could face up to seven years in prison.

Officials did not name the businesses raided by police. Reporters from the AFP news agency saw officers leading a woman in handcuffs the Have A Nice Stay bookshop into a van.

The shop in the city's densely packed Mong Kok area was founded in 2022 by a group of former journalists, stocking literature on democracy, authoritarianism and media literacy.

The raid came a day after it announced it would be shutting down in August, citing financial reasons and what it called an "elusive 'red line'" over what material is considered problematic.

On its Facebook page, the shop says it stocks books from Hong Kong and Taiwan, covering "literature, history, philosophy, art, sociology and self-improvement".

Neither business is attending this year's Hong Kong Book Fair, which opened on Wednesday.

There have been two other raids on bookshops in Hong Kong in 2026. Two workers were arrested at the Hunter store in June, and a further four were arrested from Book Punch in March.

Amnesty International said the raids indicated "the chilling reality of what the city has become: a place where you can be criminalised simply for what's on your bookshelf".

It said uncertainty over "so-called 'red lines'" had left booksellers and writers "guessing which titles could lead to criminal investigation, arrest or closure" - resulting in fear and self-censorship.
body.zh: 警方突袭两家独立书店后，五名涉嫌在香港出售和展示被视为“煽动”书籍的人被捕。 当局表示，这些出版物煽动了对该领土政府、司法和执法机构的“仇恨”。政府在一份声明中表示，警察从两家商店没收了书籍。 该团伙包括两名年龄在 37 岁和 57 岁之间的男性，以及三名年龄在 30 岁到 59 岁之间的女性，涉嫌“具有煽动意图”，违反国家安全法。 目前，他们已被拘留接受调查。如果罪名成立，他们可能面临最高七年的监禁。 官员们没有透露警方突击搜查的企业名称。法新社记者看到，警察将一名戴着手铐的妇女带进了一辆面包车。 这家商店位于香港人口稠密的旺角区，由一群前记者于 2022 年创立，出售有关民主、威权主义和媒体素养的书籍。 这次突袭是在该公司宣布将于 8 月份关闭的一天后进行的，理由是财务原因以及所谓的“难以捉摸的‘红线’”，即哪些材料被认为有问题。 该书店在其Facebook页面上称，其库存来自香港和台湾的书籍，涵盖“文学、历史、哲学、艺术、社会学和自我提升”。 两家公司都没有参加今年于周三开幕的香港书展。 2026 年，香港还发生了两起针对书店的突袭行动。6 月，Hunter 书店有两名员工被捕，3 月 Book Punch 又有四名员工被捕。 国际特赦组织表示，这次突袭表明“这座城市已经变成了一个令人毛骨悚然的现实：一个你可能仅仅因为书架上的东西就被定罪的地方”。 报告称，“所谓‘红线’”的不确定性让书商和作家“猜测哪些书名可能导致刑事调查、逮捕或关闭”，从而导致恐惧和自我审查。

reflection.en: When authorities use their power to suppress ideas and silence voices, it can feel like a heavy burden on the people. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us that the character of those in power deeply impacts the well-being of society. In such times, we pray for leaders who govern with justice and compassion, fostering an environment where all can thrive.
reflection.zh: 当掌权者利用权力压制思想、噤声异议时，这会给民众带来沉重负担。箴言28:15提醒我们，掌权者的品格深刻影响着社会的福祉。在这样的时刻，我们为那些以公义和怜悯治理的领袖祷告，愿他们能营造一个让所有人都能蓬勃发展的环境。

title.en: China economic growth falls sharply, missing target
title.zh: 中国经济增长大幅下滑，未能达到目标

summary.en: China's economic growth has significantly slowed, missing its target due to weak domestic demand and the impact of the Iran war on global oil prices, despite strong export performance.
summary.zh: 由于国内需求疲软以及伊朗战争对油价的影响，中国经济增长大幅放缓，未能达到预期目标，尽管出口表现强劲。

body.en:
China's economic growth slowed sharply between the start of April and end of June as weak domestic demand and the Iran war's impact on oil prices overshadowed the country's strong exports.

Official gross domestic product (GDP) figures showed the world's second largest economy grew in the second quarter by 4.3%, below Beijing's annual target, and after a 5% rise in the first quarter.

It comes a day after separate data showed China's exports had jumped by 27% in June compared to a year earlier.

In March, China cut the growth target to a range of 4.5%-5% , its lowest economic expansion goal since 1991, a move some analysts say has given Beijing space to acknowledge pre-existing economic weakness.

The announcement represents the first full quarter of GDP data since the start of the Iran war on 28 February and marks the lowest quarterly expansion since the end of 2022, as China was emerging from its strict Covid-19 restrictions.

"The are more external instability and uncertainty factors," China's National Bureau of Statistics said in a release accompanying the figures.

It also noted an imbalance between strong supply and weak demand in the domestic economy.

Separate data released on Wednesday highlighted the economic challenges Beijing is facing at home - including a long-running property market slump and weak consumer spending.

New home prices contracted again, although the 0.1% fall in June was at a slightly slower pace than the previous month.

Fabien Yip, a market analyst at investment platform IG told the BBC that China's businesses are absorbing higher energy and raw materials costs "because demand at the till is too weak to bear it".

The situation will become more difficult to manage the longer the Iran war goes on, she added.

However Capital Economics's head of China economics Julian Evans-Pritchard said the actual slowdown in the country's economy may have less to do with changing conditions, and more to do with a change in the national growth target which had "given the authorities more room to acknowledge the reality on the ground".

"This may largely represent a greater willingness to acknowledge pre-existing weakness rather than a sudden deterioration in underlying growth," he said, noting that the official figure is now closer in line with Capital's own estimate of Chinese growth.

"If that's the case, then the GDP figures should not be interpreted as a sign that the economy is suddenly slowing sharply. The June data also offer some reassurance, with improvements across all indicators."

Customs data for June, which was released on Tuesday, showed that China's tech exports were boosted by soaring global demand for semiconductors to power artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

body.zh: 由于国内需求疲软和伊朗战争对油价的影响掩盖了中国强劲的出口，中国的经济增长在四月初至六月底大幅放缓。 官方国内生产总值(GDP)数据显示，继第一季度增长5%之后，世界第二大经济体第二季度增长4.3%，低于北京的年度目标。 一天前，政府数据显示，中国 6 月份出口同比增长 27%。 3月份，中国将增长目标下调至4.5%-5%，这是自1991年以来的最低经济扩张目标，一些分析师表示，此举让官员在管理经济方面拥有更大的灵活性。 该公告代表了自 2 月 28 日伊朗战争爆发以来第一个完整季度的 GDP 数据，也标志着中国正在摆脱严格的 Covid-19 限制之际，自 2022 年底以来的最低季度扩张。 “外部不稳定和不确定因素较多，”中国国家统计局在发布的数据中表示。 报告还指出，国内经济供给旺盛与需求疲软之间存在不平衡。 周三公布的另一份数据突显了北京在国内面临的经济挑战，包括房地产市场长期低迷和消费者支出疲软。 新房价格再次收缩，但 6 月份降幅为 0.1%，降幅较上月略有放缓。 投资平台IG的市场分析师Fabien Yip告诉BBC，中国企业正在吸收更高的能源和原材料成本，“因为收银台的需求太弱而无法承受”。 她补充说，伊朗战争持续的时间越长，局势就越难以控制。 周二公布的 6 月份海关数据显示，全球对为人工智能 (AI) 数据中心提供动力的半导体需求飙升，推动了中国的科技出口。 中国电动汽车（EV）需求的激增也极大地推动了中国的出口——每月汽车出口量首次突破100万辆。

title.en: Nearly two million evacuated as Typhoon Bavi barrels towards China
title.zh: 强台风巴威逼近中国，近两百万人被疏散

summary.en: A powerful typhoon, Bavi, is approaching China, prompting the evacuation of nearly two million people. In the Philippines, heavy rains associated with the storm have already caused two landslides, resulting in 17 fatalities.
summary.zh: 强台风巴威正逼近中国，导致近两百万人被疏散。在菲律宾，受台风带来的强降雨影响，已发生两起山体滑坡，造成17人死亡。

body.en:
China evacuated more than 1.8 million people on Saturday as Typhoon Bavi churned toward the major eastern city of Wenzhou after pummelling Japan's southern Sakishima island chain with heavy rain and violent winds and brushing past northern Taiwan.

Even as Bavi continues to slow and weaken on its northwesterly path over cooler seas, the typhoon is still a potent risk due to the sheer volume of moisture it holds within its rain bands, about the size of France from end to end.

Bavi had maximum sustained winds of 144 km/h, equivalent to Category 1 on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, and was about 200km southeast of Wenling in the eastern province of Zhejiang as of Saturday night (AEST), according to the National Meteorological Center.

Bavi is forecast to make landfall around Wenzhou, home to some 10 million people, early on Sunday.

State media said more than 1.7 million people had been evacuated across Zhejiang province, where Wenzhou is located, and more than 100,000 in neighbouring Fujian province.

"I'm a little worried, but I think it'll be OK. We've been through typhoons before. We'll get through it," said Wenzhou resident Huang Xinghuan, 50, who was out buying groceries at a traditional wet market before it closed ahead of the typhoon.

Huang said his family had stocked about two to three days' worth of water. "I think supplies are well guaranteed now. There's no need to panic or stockpile a lot of food or other supplies," he added.

While Japan and Taiwan have not so far reported any deaths from the typhoon, 17 people died in the Philippines due to heavy rains brought by an enhanced southwest monsoon, worsened by Bavi's impact.

Taiwan's fire department said 87 people had been injured, mostly falls from motorcycles or bicycles, as well as people falling over or being struck by objects.

More than 18,000 households and facilities across Okinawa, Japan lost power as the typhoon pounded Japan's remote southwestern islands, with the Miyako region hardest hit.

Japanese airlines cancelled dozens of flights, affecting more than 26,000 passengers.

"Miyako is taking worst of typhoon Bavi," professional storm-chaser James Reynolds posted on X from Ishigaki on Saturday.

"Conditions on Ishigaki gale force with some overnight gusts to typhoon strength."

In Taiwan, the government evacuated more than 14,000 people from mainly mountainous areas as the island shut down for the approach of Bavi to the north.

title.en: 'Sensitive little guys': The problem with the greater glider's not-so-great glide

summary.en: The endangered species' glide distance is less than half of what was previously assumed. Scientists say it puts them at risk.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In 1941 in Milton, a village in southern NSW, a local reported seeing a greater glider, a native 'flying marsupial', soar through the night air to land 100m away.

The one sighting launched a pervasive myth about the abilities of the greater glider, one of 10 glider species native to Australia.

"It was a misidentification that has carried on for many decades, and there actually just is no dataset or empirical measurements," Dr Ana Gracanin told SBS News.

Gracanin, a researcher with the Fenner School of Environment and Society at the Australian National University, set out with a team to measure the greater glider's glide distance for the first time.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The southern greater glider, named 'great' because of its size, soared an average of only 19.1m, or less than a quarter the distance it was once assumed.

The researchers say their findings have big implications for the conservation of the endangered species.

Gracanin spent hours in the forest at night with infrared cameras and torches, becoming familiar with the individual gliders and their favourite tree dents.

"My friends have a joke because they all look very similar ... whenever there's a glider, we'd be like 'It's Gary! We have a Gary!'"

It's unclear what the total population of southern greater gliders is, but scientists estimate their population declined by 80 per cent after the Black Summer bushfires.

"Often they're very high up in the canopies, but if you put your binoculars to your eyes you can very quickly tell if it's a greater glider," Gracinan said.

"It has huge fluffy ears, a very funny gremlin-y face, and they have a very long fluffy tail ... They're just a big ball of fluff."

Recording data on the southern greater gliders' movements for the first time, Gracinan and her team found they climbed an average of 22m before launching themselves at a 43.5 degree angle at a nearby tree.

"It kind of goes into a Superman pose and has its hands under its chin ... like a black furry flying carpet shape that goes through the sky, and the tail is spinning left, right, left to stabilize."

The longest glide they recorded was 47m. But the average distance was well short of that, at 19.1m.

The distance fell short of the glider record, which was set by a yellow-bellied glider which travelled 145m.

The southern greater glider's inability to glide long distances puts them at greater risk of becoming isolated from the rest of the population, and of extinction.

"They're restricted to their little territories, their gliding ability and their diet," Gracanin said.

body.zh: 1941 年，在新南威尔士州南部的一个村庄米尔顿，当地人报告看到一只更大的滑翔机，一种本土的“飞行有袋动物”，在夜间空中翱翔，降落在 100 米外。 这次目击事件引发了关于大滑翔机能力的普遍神话，大滑翔机是澳大利亚本土的 10 种滑翔机之一。 Ana Gracanin 博士告诉 SBS 新闻：“这是一种错误的识别，已经持续了几十年，而且实际上没有数据集或经验测量。” 澳大利亚国立大学芬纳环境与社会学院的研究员格拉卡宁带领一个团队首次测量了大型滑翔机的滑翔距离。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 南方大型滑翔机因其体型而被称为“伟大”，其平均飞行高度仅为 19.1m，不到原来假设距离的四分之一。 研究人员表示，他们的发现对保护濒危物种具有重大意义。 格拉卡宁晚上带着红外摄像机和手电筒在森林里待了几个小时，逐渐熟悉了个体滑翔机和它们最喜欢的树凹。 “我的朋友们有一个笑话，因为他们看起来都非常相似......每当有滑翔机时，我们都会说‘这是加里！我们有一个加里！’” 目前还不清楚南部大滑翔机的总数量是多少，但科学家估计，黑夏丛林大火之后，它们的数量减少了 80%。 格拉西南说：“它们通常在树冠的高处，但如果你把双筒望远镜放在眼前，你就能很快看出它是否是一架更大的滑翔机。” “它有巨大的毛茸茸的耳朵，一张非常有趣的小妖精般的脸，还有一条很长的毛茸茸的尾巴……它们只是一个大毛球。” Gracinan 和她的团队首次记录了南方大滑翔机的运动数据，发现它们平均爬升 22 m，然后以 43.5 度角发射到附近的一棵树上。 “它有点像超人的姿势，双手放在下巴下面……就像一条黑色毛茸茸的飞毯形状穿过天空，尾巴左右旋转以稳定。” 他们记录的最长滑翔距离为47m。但平均距离远低于此，为 19.1m。 这一距离低于由黄腹滑翔机创下的滑翔机记录，飞行距离为 145m。 南方大滑翔机无法长距离滑翔，这使得它们面临与其他种群隔离和灭绝的更大风险。 “它们的领地、滑翔能力和饮食都受到限制，”格拉卡宁说。 栖息地的丧失意味着更大的滑翔机很难找到成熟的老树来栖息......

title.en: Australian patient details exposed in GP network cyberattack
title.zh: 澳大利亚患者详细信息在全科医生网络网络攻击中暴露

summary.en: Partnered Health said that 21 clinics across several Australian cities had been affected by a cybersecurity breach.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Thousands of medical records and patient information stored with a giant healthcare provider have been breached in a cyber attack.

Partnered Health, owned by private equity firm Quadrant, said 21 clinics across several cities including Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra have been affected by the breach on 23 June.

"Our investigations to date have confirmed that personal information (including health information) was taken from some of the clinics in our network," the healthcare provider said on Wednesday.

"As a health services provider, we know our patients and our people trust us with personal and medical information, and we sincerely apologise for any concern and inconvenience this may cause them."

The healthcare group said "a malicious actor" accessed the data, prompting it to report the incident to the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, and law enforcement.

Personal information stolen included names, dates of birth, addresses and contact details as well as Medicare, private health insurance and concession card details.

Medical information and treatment details, including consultation notes, referral letters, and pathology or diagnostic results recorded by a GP were also breached.

The medical group has sought an interim injunction from the Supreme Court of NSW ordering that the accessed data is not used or published.

Established in 2013, Partnered Health has more than 60 medical centres nationwide as well as skin cancer, allied health and mental health clinics, with its services reaching more than five million people.

Health insurer Bupa announced in June it was acquiring Partnered Health, the latest major business to be struck by hackers.

Data breach notifications to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner reached a record high in 2025, with major incidents including a cyberattack on Qantas that compromised the details of 5.7 million customers and reportedly leaked on the dark web.

The office said it received 1205 data breach notifications in the 2025 calendar year, representing an eight per cent increase from 2024.

title.en: Deadly avian flu detected in New Zealand for the first time
title.zh: 新西兰首次发现致命禽流感

summary.en: The alert followed a migratory seabird near Wellington returning a postive test result.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
New Zealand has reported its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu after a migratory seabird found on a ‌beach near Wellington tested positive.

The case in a ‌brown skua seabird comes after the virus was detected in June in Australia , the last continent to ‌report the virus.

The virulent H5 strain has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions and infecting poultry and dairy farms as well as some farm workers.

"There is no evidence of any mass mortality in wildlife or transmission between wild birds in New Zealand. There has been no detection ‌in poultry," Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said in ⁠a statement on Wednesday.

Hoggard said New Zealand might see a similar pattern to cases reported in Australia , where there have been 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu as of Wednesday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

New Zealand has been preparing for the arrival of H5N1, working with the poultry industry to develop biosecurity and resilience plans.

New Zealand's wild birds are unusually vulnerable because they evolved for millions ⁠of years without native land mammals, leaving many species ‌flightless, ground-nesting and poorly equipped to defend themselves against predators.

That isolation made them unique but also left them highly exposed to habitat ‌loss and introduced pests such as stoats, rats and feral cats.

Many species are already endangered, putting them at great risk of extinction if the virus spreads rapidly.

Health officials have started a vaccination program for 300 core breeding birds from five of the country's most endangered species, including flightless takahe and kakapo.

Brett Gartrell, professor of wildlife health at Massey University, told Reuters ‌he was worried that bird flu could push some of the country's critically endangered birds to extinction.

"We are incredibly worried about New Zealand's biodiversity because our birds have never had to deal with anything like this before," Gartrell said.

"If it spreads quickly in New Zealand, we could be in trouble ... those core group of birds that (officials) want to protect with the vaccination won't be fully immune if it spreads too quickly."

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's shift towards tougher artificial intelligence regulation has been broadly welcomed, but pressure is building for more detail and decisive action on the risks posed by the technology.

Albanese announced on Wednesday the federal government would legislate a set of AI standards next year, including new requirements for data centres to underwrite energy generation and pay for additional water use.

An AI office would be created within Albanese's department, while national standards would cover education and training, workplace rights and productivity. The government also wants to fast-track AI investment in Australia.

The announcement marks a shift away from the federal government's previous light-touch approach to regulation, and comes after months of pressure from both the tech industry and those worried about the rapid shifts of AI on the economy.

But the prime minister provided few details about the proposals which he vowed to legislate by early 2027 after a national cabinet process with state and territory leaders.

Albanese said getting the framework right would enable faster approvals and make Australia a more attractive destination for international investors.

"It is not our goal to try and legislate for every possible eventuality or risk," he said.

Monash University AI researcher Geoff Webb labelled the AI office an "important initiative" that would bolster Australia's capacity to pursue "critical" sovereign AI capabilities.

Digital Rights Watch chair Lizzie O'Shea also backed the move but was concerned fast-tracking AI data centre approvals could exacerbate community mistrust in AI.

"[By] prioritising data centres, we lose capacity to build out renewable energy projects in the climate crisis, new home construction in the housing crisis, and we likely increase the current cost of electricity and water in a cost of living crisis," O'Shea said.

But Greens senator David Shoebridge was critical, saying the office would not have statutory powers.

"What the prime minister has offered today is a single door in his office," he said. "That is not going to deliver the protections Australians have been asking for."

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said the office would create “more bureaucracy” and hinder Australia’s adoption of the technology.

The government released expectations for large AI data centres in March, but Albanese said these would now be strengthened through legislation.
